question.problem:
Let ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{128}$ be a random sample of size $n=128$ from a population with a population mean $\mu =250$ and population standard deviation $\sigma =64.$ Find an approximation for the probability that the sample mean is less than $260.$

*Hint: A table of values of $Φ(z)$ for different values of $z$ is given below, where $Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution. *

| $z$ | $\,0.06\,$ | $\,0.07\,$ | $\,0.08\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,1.6\,$ | $\,0.9515\,$ | $\,0.9525\,$ | $\,0.9535\,$ |
| $\,1.7\,$ | $\,0.9608\,$ | $\,0.9616\,$ | $\,0.9625\,$ |
| $\,1.8\,$ | $\,0.9686\,$ | $\,0.9693\,$ | $\,0.9699\,$ |
question.worked_solution:
Suppose that ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{n}$ is a random sample of size $n$ from a population with a population mean $\mu $ and population standard deviation $\sigma .$ The central limit theorem (or CLT) states that for sufficiently large $n,$ the distribution of the sample mean $\overset{―}{X}$ can be approximated as 

$$
\overset{―}{X}∼N\,(\mu ,\frac{{\sigma }^{2}}{n}).
$$

In our case, we have

$$
n=128,\,\mu =250,\,\sigma =64.
$$

Therefore, by the CLT, we have that the distribution of the sample mean can be approximated as

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{X} & ∼N\,(\mu ,\frac{{\sigma }^{2}}{n}) \\  & ∼N\,(250,\frac{{64}^{2}}{128}) \\  & ∼N(250,32).\end{aligned}
$$

We want to find $P(\overset{―}{X}<260).$ So, we convert $\overset{―}{X}$ to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(\overset{―}{X}<260) & =P(Z<\frac{260-250}{\sqrt{32}}) \\  & =P(Z<\frac{5}{2\sqrt{2}}) \\  & ≈P(Z<1.77) \\  & =Φ(1.77)\end{aligned}
$$

From the table, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}Φ(1.77)=0.9616.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(\overset{―}{X}<260) & =Φ(1.77) \\  & =0.9616.\end{aligned}
$$
